s0362: An SMS from the “Bank Security Service”
s0363:
Otabek is a client of “Samo Bank” (the name is fictional) and has an Uzcard card. One day he received the following SMS on his phone:

“Dear Samo Bank client! A failure occurred on the bank's server, and your card data have been erased. Because of this, your card has been temporarily blocked. Most importantly, your account is no longer safe! To unblock your card within 24 hours, follow the link and enter your card number, expiry date, and the SMS code that will be sent to your phone: samobank-uz.help/karta”

(The message and link are made up.)
s0364: Recognize a fraud (phishing) message and judge the right action
s0365: Check each piece of advice: does it give card information to the unknown sender of the message, or does it contact the bank in a trusted way?
s0366:
Which of the following pieces of advice are right for Otabek? Choose the row that gives the correct “Yes” or “No” answer for each.
1) Reply to the SMS and send the card information and SMS code.
2) Call the number shown on the back of the card or in the bank's official app himself and ask about this message.
3) If the address in the link looks like the bank's name, follow the link and do what it says.
s0371: Warning signs: rushing, scaring, SMS code
s0372: “Within 24 hours”, “not safe”, and asking for an SMS code are typical signs of a fraud message.
s0374: A bank never asks for an SMS code; a person who gives out the code opens the card to a scammer.
s0375: 2) Call the official number himself → Yes
s0376: If he takes the number from the card or the official app, not from the message, he will be talking to the real bank.
s0378: Scammers create fake addresses that look very similar to the bank's name; looking similar is not a sign of safety.
s0380: With a suspicious message, contact only the bank itself, through an official channel.
s0381: An address in a link that looks like the bank's name does not mean it is real; fake websites are made exactly like that.
s0382: You should never send the SMS code and card information to anyone, but calling the bank's official number is good advice.
s0383: A bank does not ask for an SMS code; sending the code leads to losing the money on the card.
s0384: A message that rushes you and asks for an SMS code is almost always fraud. Contact the bank only through its official number.
